The entire Star Wars universe is a case of "Pick your poison". Here's another for you, the conflict of Jedi v Sith. Jedi saw the Force as a religio-mystical influence, and themselves as an Order that had to be harnessed for the furtherance of good for all (Collectivism). The Sith, meanwhile, were quite honest with themselves about what any rational human would do with such a tool at their disposal; He did what any human does with tools, and uses them to further his own ends (Individualism). The Jedi will point to the Sith and say "They tried to use Order 66 to have us all genocided! They had the Younglings slaughtered..." and while that may be true, who were the originators of this Millennia-spanning genocide campaign? If we look back into the annals of the Jedi Order, we find that the Sith were spawned from a faction of Jedi that were exiled from the Order by a bunch of fundamentalists that refused to consider an alternate interpretation of their ideology, that the Force was not just something to passively accept and contemplate, but a tool to use for your own ends. It was then that the Jedi began an extermination campaign of their own against their former brothers now tellingly named the "Dark Jedi," now known as the Sith, long before the fall of the Galactic Republic and the rise of Darth Sidious to power. Finally, we can take a look at each order's code of honor...

There is no emotion, there is peace.

There is no ignorance, there is knowledge.

There is no passion, there is serenity.

There is no chaos, there is harmony.

There is no death, there is the Force.

Versus

Peace is a lie, there is only Passion

Through Passion, I gain Strength

Through Strength, I gain Power

Through Power, I gain Victory

Through Victory, my chains are broken

The Force shall set me Free

One of these codes blinds the adherent to the realities of the Nietzschean will-to-power, and the other embraces it, whilst leaving the implicative ethics of that embracing up to the adherent. In the end, the Force is quite demonstrably a tool like any other ability humanity has at it's disposal, a tool that can be used for "Good" or for "Evil", much like a blaster or a lightsaber. Context is everything. It is, however, the Sith that are honest about the nature of this conflict, and while the Jedi require ignorance of the nature of this conflict, as they say, "Truth will always out."

Ever wonder why, despite the claimed validity of the Jedi Temple's ideology, they keep "losing students to the Dark Side"? Here's the key to understanding that issue between the two schools. They aren't "stumbling", they're discovering that their elders have been keeping them conveniently and dogmatically ignorant, then telling them ignorance doesn't exist in a verbal shell game. Power, whether political or Force-based, is a tool. But like any tool, it falls incumbent upon the user not to lose themselves to that tool, lest it destroy them, as the path of the Sith has the very real capability to do.

In the end, you can choose to walk the razor's edge, or remain dogmatically ignorant about the realities of the universe. Pick your poison.

This is a lot more than "bundling." It seems like not many people decided to read the article, and I would encourage you to do so.

Kaspersky is protesting because of a few specific behaviors that IMNSHO are actually very valid.

  • Windows 10 auto-uninstalling anti-virus programs that it does not like. This may be necessary in some cases, but the option not to do this is apparently ignored by Windows 10. Note that this is not the only program or program type this happens to, and it sucks.

  • The notice that anti-virus protection has expired is disabled after a few days, Windows Defender is turned on, and your original anti-virus is left to rot, more or less.

  • Anti-virus developers having little to no time to adjust their products to Windows 10 at release. I remember seeing several anti-virus packages having some serious problems with Windows 10 to start with. Kaspersky is generally pretty on top of things, so to see them having a problem like this is IMO an indicator that something is wrong.

  • Windows warning screens apparently encourage people to enable Windows Defender, which disables third party packages, even if a third party package is active, up-to-date, and operational.

Not all of Kaspersky's comments are wise here. One of his proposed remedies, for example, involves delaying Windows major updates for anti-virus companies to be able to update their programs. This has some bad implications, there, and may well not be necessary thanks to the Windows Insider program. I am unfamiliar with the details of Windows Insider, but the author says it is unclear as to why this would be insufficient for adapting anti-virus software. However, this goes way beyond just "bundling" Defender with Windows. He also cites some other types of software that meet a similar fate, that are frequently rendered useless by Windows updates, such as VPN software.

Now, it is possible the article is inaccurate, but from what I was able to glean, some of his grievances at the very least are valid.
